newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan king discusses W.Sahara with U.N. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan king discusses W.Sahara with U.N. envoy.

text.p: King Hassan of Morocco conferred with U.N. envoy for Western Sahara James Baker on the U.N. peace plan in the disputed territory, a Moroccan official said on Thursday.

"King Hassan II held a working session with U.N. envoy James Baker on the U.N. peace plan in the (Western) Sahara and latest developments in the region," said the official, who declined to be identified.

The meeting took place at the royal residence of Bouznika, south of Rabat on Wednesday evening, he said. It was attended by Morocco's Crown Prince Sidi Mohammmed and senior officials, he said but gave no other details.

The former U.S. Secretary of State was appointed by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan last month to try to resolve the dispute over the former Spanish colony. It is claimed by Morocco while the Algerian-backed Polisario Front seeks independence.
The U.N. envoy, who arrived in Rabat early on Wednesday, told reporters his visit was a "fact-finding trip" on the disputed territory.
"During this trip I will be primarily listening to all parties...I am here to listen," Baker said.
A ceasefire, monitored by a U.N. force, has held since September 1991 but plans for a U.N. referendum on the future of the territory have been stalled since January 1992 over who is eligible to vote.

Baker was expected to meet Moroccan officials at the interior and foreign ministries on Thursday, the official added. The U.N. envoy, who is travelling on a Spanish military airplane, will leave for Algiers on Friday, officials said.
